correctness.rationale: Rechecked the repaired claim rather than the removed perturbation finding. Expanding V gives y²/2+xy/2+3x²/4+Bx⁴/4; its derivative is exactly −(y²+x²+Bx⁴)/2+ε(y+x/2)cos t. The Young bound with coefficient 1/8 costs (5/2)ε², and V≤y²+x²+Bx⁴. Thus limsup V≤(20/3)ε²<8ε² and every trajectory enters the invariant sublevel V≤8ε² in finite time; this uses the strict gap and not eventual strict inequality at the limsup bound itself. Forward completeness follows for the planar polynomial ODE by coercivity and for z by integration. In the sublevel, x_i²≤(64/5)ε², so B(x₁²+x₁x₂+x₂²)≤3/20. Direct differentiation of the difference form W gives the claimed identity and W′≤−W/4; its norm contracts at rate 1/8. The period map contracts a complete invariant sublevel, giving existence, and absorption upgrades this to global attraction and uniqueness. The half-period symmetry follows by periodic uniqueness. Pairing halves gives the exact signed sinh average, strict for β≠0 since X is not identically zero. The smooth axial observable on the absorbing range transfers the planar error into an absolutely integrable transient whose tail is O(e^(−t/8)). Phase translation preserves the estimates and the period mean, ruling out compact forward-invariant sets in the phase extension for β≠0. At β=0 the mean vanishes and the same expansion in time gives boundedness. The original small-amplitude formula is also correct: the cubic fundamental correction solves L U=−sin³t and is proportional to cos t, orthogonal to sin t; the moment coefficients are 1/2 and 3/8. It is no longer presented as an original result. The archival verification script was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The cutoff is a sufficient weak-drive condition only; the estimate is asymptotic in time with an initial-condition-dependent constant. The single-well assumption B≥0 is used in the coercivity and contraction estimates.
